start_here: Say to your AI: "Start a computer on my spare Linux machine at 192.0.2.40 as computer.example.com, have it fetch and build its engine itself, and tell me whether its health page answers 200."
no_lists_because: It keeps no list of yours: it reads a request file, the computer row and provider descriptions it names, and keeps one lease file.
instructions: 1. Write request.json: lease_file, machine {provider (the path of a provider description file, here one for a machine you already run), name, placement {address}}, name {host_name}, ssh {known_hosts}, computer_row (or computer_row_file: the computer's own record:computer row, whose runs names its units). Paths are read relative to the file.

2. Say the line in start_here. Your AI reads this tool's row with tools:list {tool: "tool:start-a-computer"} and runs node tools/start-a-computer/do-work/start-a-computer.mjs start request.json. For a rented machine the provider credential (vault key from the machine row) goes on descriptor 3 and the DNS credential on descriptor 4, never in argv.

3. Read the one JSON line it prints: lease, host_name, arch, price, applied (what was written, built and restarted) and health_status. A first build of an engine takes a while on a small machine; if it stops part way, run the same command again: the saved lease resumes it and a commit already built is not built again.
4. Run tool:check-a-sign-up against https://<host_name> to prove a new account can sign up, and tool:give-back-a-computer with the lease file when you stop paying for it.

worked_examples.title: A computer started on a machine the person already runs, its engine built there
worked_examples.ask: Start a computer on my spare machine and tell me if its health page answers.
worked_examples.given: From tools/start-a-computer/test/start-a-computer.test.mjs ('starting a computer on an adopted machine sets it up, has it fetch and build its engine itself, serves and reads it back'). request.json = {"lease_file":"lease.json","machine":{"provider":"providers/adopted-machine.json","name":"a-pi","placement":{"address":"192.0.2.40"}},"name":{"host_name":"computer.example.com"},"ssh":{"known_hosts":"known_hosts"},"computer_row":{"address":"192.0.2.41","name":"example-computer","runs":{"health_listen":"127.0.0.1:7199","health":{"path":"/readyz","status":200,"where":"machine","host":"computer.example.com"},"units":[{"unit":"example-computer.service","template":"tools/keep-an-engine-on-a-computer/serve-computer.service","user":"example-computer","state":"/var/lib/example-computer","builds":"/var/lib/example-computer/builds","program":"example-engine","key_file":"/var/lib/example-computer/computer.key","folders":["/var/lib/example-computer/persons"],"settings_file":"/etc/example-computer/computer.json","settings":{"listen":"127.0.0.1:7199","persons":"/var/lib/example-computer/persons","computer_key_file":"/var/lib/example-computer/computer.key","public_origin":"https://computer.example.com"},"source":{"repository":"https://git.example.test/example-engine.git","commit":"cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc","build":["cargo","build","--locked","--release"],"output":"{builds}/target/release/example-engine","environment":["HOME={state}"]}}]}}}. The machine reports aarch64, the engine at cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc is not built there yet, and https://computer.example.com/readyz answers 200. Run: node tools/start-a-computer/do-work/start-a-computer.mjs start request.json
worked_examples.hands_back: {"lease":{"provider":"adopted-machine","name":"a-pi","address":"192.0.2.40","state":"running"},"host_name":"computer.example.com","arch":"aarch64","price":null,"applied":{"built":[{"unit":"example-computer.service","from":null,"commit":"cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc"}],"booted":["example-computer.service"],...},"health_status":200}: price is null because no monthly_price_cents was given for a machine the person already runs, the machine fetched that commit from the row's address and built it, and health_status 200 means the public /readyz page answered.
